analysis: The PR modifies only docs/architecture/inference.md. The patch (head lines 2172-2184) adds a Flint paragraph describing constrained chaining in the CBv2 engine, a mask cache keyed by constraint state, and adding RecursiveSI/flint-int4 to the automatic paged list at legacy serving width on M5 Pro/Max/Ultra. The supplied units, head lines 1-797, contain unchanged Nemotron Super, GLM5Next and managed-slot documentation, and the changed range lies outside them. I reviewed that surrounding text against the threat model (T-041 prefix-cache scope and TTL, TB-007 inference engine, A-001 prompts) and found no inconsistencies. The text is consistent with T-041. Prefix reuse is partitioned by the authenticated cache scope and off without one. The slot emits no cache receipts. The SSD cache posture and TTL are not altered. No code, key handling, attestation, encryption, authorization or billing behavior changes. The new Flint paragraph is outside the supplied excerpts, so I could not review it directly. It claims token streams identical to unchained decode, which is a correctness claim, not a security control. The device mask cache is keyed by constraint state and holds no prompt-derived content on disk. A mild residual question for the next pass is whether a shared mask cache across requests could create a cross-request timing channel. That is speculative and unsupported by the visible evidence. No threat-model update is needed for documentation alone. I set needs_deeper_review false: the changed lines are docs-only and I identified no concrete security regression.
